method: Independence weighting (current, Nov 2 2026): each Yea/Nay vote is weighted 2.0 when the member votes against their own party's majority, 0.5 on a pure party-line vote (the two party majorities split and the member votes with their own), and 1.0 otherwise (both majorities agree and the member goes along). Indicator score = 10 × weighted aligned votes ÷ weighted votes cast; composite = mean of indicators. Party leadership is approximated by each party's majority on the roll call; independents count with the party they caucus with.

New indicator F (fiscal / consensus-spending restraint): cross-party, high-stakes votes where majorities of both parties voted Yea. House: NDAA FY26 final (S.1071), FY26 minibus (H.R.6938), Consolidated Appropriations 2026 passage (H.R.7148), MilCon-VA FY27 (H.R.8469). Senate: NDAA FY26 (S.2296), NDAA FY26 final cloture (S.1071), MilCon-VA FY26 (H.R.3944), FY26 minibus (H.R.6938), CR FY27 (H.R.6500). The framework position on these is Nay. Candidate CR, omnibus and NDAA roll calls on which a majority of Democrats voted Nay were not added because they were not cross-party (House 2025 roll calls 70 and 285; 2026 roll calls 53, 247, 272 and 278; Senate roll calls 133, 618 and 679). No Senate FISA roll call was found in the data used (gap). No standalone debt-limit vote took place in the 119th (the increase rode in the party-line reconciliation bill), and no standalone war-powers or supplemental vote met the both-majorities test.

Green (tightened): weighted composite ≥ 7.0 AND uniparty count below the flag AND no scorable indicator below 3. Yellow: 4.0–6.9, or ≥ 7.0 failing a Green test (the reason is shown on the card). Red < 4.0. Gray: non-voting delegate, fewer than 50% of scored votes cast, or fewer than 5 indicators scorable.
Previous method (kept on each card as 'Previous equal-weight'): every vote weighted 1.0, Green = composite ≥ 7.0, and no F indicator.

Correction: the earlier uniparty counts for House members were inflated by a parsing bug (House Yea/Nay labels were not recognized when computing party majorities, so every House scored Yea counted as uniparty). Counts are now recomputed for all members; Senate counts are unchanged.
Downgrade rule: a Green would drop to Yellow if direct contributions from country-focused PACs were ≥ 5% of receipts. No member triggered it.
Uniparty count: scored roll calls where the member voted Yea and majorities of both parties also voted Yea (bipartisan-consensus measure, not a judgment). Flag at ≥ 10 (House) / ≥ 8 (Senate).
Independents are scored individually and grouped with the party they caucus with for clustering; party shown as I.
Vote cut-offs: House roll calls through Sep 16, 2026 (clerk.house.gov); Senate through Sep 30, 2026 (Voteview data; links point to senate.gov).

Money: FEC bulk files for the 2025–26 cycle (weball26 totals, pas226 PAC-to-candidate; refunds netted, so small residuals can appear). Top 3 PAC donors and top 2 country-focused entries per member shown.

Stock trades: House PTRs from the House Clerk financial-disclosure index and ptr-pdfs (2025–2026, parsed from the PDFs; index checked Nov 4, 2026); Senate PTRs from eFD (efdsearch.senate.gov) via a public calendar-2025 mirror. 156 members matched (129 House, 27 Senate): 931 filings, 9,066 transactions. Up to 3 notable trades per member, taken as the largest by amount range; House PDFs often cut off the upper bound, shown as '$X+'. Committee-sector overlap is a ticker-to-sector map (defense, energy, health/pharma, financial, tech/telecom, agriculture) matched to committee jurisdiction: 48 members have one or more overlapping transactions. This is factual overlap only.

X posts: official handles from the unitedstates/congress-legislators social file, verified with the X user lookup (490 found, 483 government-verified). Recent posts (Oct 3 – Nov 4, 2026) were fetched with keyword searches; 494 posts from 205 members were tagged by topic (B border, A foreign aid/Ukraine/Israel, W war powers, T trade/tariffs/China, E spending/energy/economy, C privacy/surveillance, S stock-trading ban).
